statement: [CN-N1 | constraint | critical | audio-stage-4-spatial-sfx @ anc.ch3-signal.klaxon] CONTRACT-BLOCKING, and it is a lock question before it is a design question. Intent §4 promises 'no information exists only in audio' and names a 'sound captions' setting rendered in a registered HUD surface; my treatment §3 answers with three visual parity members — a sound-caption surface (hudSurfaces.ts + a new component), a one-frame audit-band ember pulse per ch3-signal klaxon (storyDirector.ts:1879-1882 fires terminalAlarm three times with no visual member), and a per-pulse OxygenMeter tick above 25 % (parity today exists only below 25 %, OxygenMeter.tsx:7,47). Every one of those carriers lives outside production-lock.json allowedPaths: main/src/story/AuditBand.tsx, main/src/components/hud/OxygenMeter.tsx, main/src/ui/hudSurfaces.ts, main/src/story/StoryCaptions.tsx, main/src/story/ux/StoryGuidanceHud.tsx (only ux/feedbackCues.ts is allowed), and production-lock.md line 68 puts 'post-processing or any visual system' out of scope. So as the lock stands, the two parity gaps I found cannot be repaired this run and the sound-caption setting cannot be built, while every new SOUND in Stage 4 and every voiced line in Stage 6 can. I will not sign a contract whose accessibility clause names a surface no lane may create. Ruling needed, one of: (a) a bounded lock expansion of exactly four files — hudSurfaces.ts (one registration), AuditBand.tsx (ember pulse), OxygenMeter.tsx (tick), and one new file main/src/story/ux/SoundCaptions.tsx — as HUD-parity paths with the same protections as feedbackCues.ts; or (b) the contract records the three as a deferred 'audio-parity' packet, intent §4's promise is marked PARTIAL for this run (klaxon cadence and oxygen cadence above 25 % remain audio-only; SFX cue captions absent), and Stage 4 may still ship because voiced lines are their own captions and the lifecycle cues have intrinsic parity in the guidance card. I recommend (a); the files are DOM, change-gated, and no post pass or camera is touched. || [CN-N2 | question | high | audio-stage-6-voice-bus @ anc.sound-caption.vocabulary] Ownership of the sound-caption strings. They are copy-adjacent (intent §4) and storyText.ts is protected, so: you own the VOCABULARY and the both-readings test; I own PRESENTATION — uppercase, the audit band's mono 12 px / 0.14em tracking (AuditBand.tsx:114-115), layer 'informational' not 'caption', 1.2 s hold / 300 ms fade, one caption per cue kind, never the bottom-centre caption home (StoryCaptions.tsx:118-119). The strings live in a table inside the sound-caption module, not in storyText.ts. Please rule the four words: [ALARM] (terminalAlarm, klaxons), [GLITCH] (storyGlitch), [IMPACT] (shipCrash), [HATCH] (station hatch). Rule also that voiced REGULATION lines get NO cue caption (the line on screen is the caption) and that lowercase story captions never enter the surface — both keep 'who is speaking' unwritten. Owner taste I flagged in my treatment: setting-only, absent from movie mode. || [CN-N3 | constraint | high | audio-stage-3-composed-sync @ anc.a1.chroma-landing] Two lifecycle rules the intent leaves open, which I ask you to freeze as contract terms. REDUCED MOTION: chased bundles chase identically under reduced motion — quantization is timing, not motion — and each member falls to its existing RM form (flash/glitch/letterbox already have them); no bundle is de-scheduled or snapped to immediate because RM is on. PAUSE / QUIT / DEEP-LINK between arming and landing: the milestone and advanceToBeat already fired at the arming tick (your 'state is never delayed'), so nothing is lost; on resume the bundle re-arms once if a transport is live, else fires immediately (today's behaviour); on quit, deep link or replay the pending target is cleared with the rest of the director state (visual law 10). No bundle ever re-quantizes after its target is published. || [CN-N4 | endorsement | medium | audio-stage-3-composed-sync @ anc.a3.first-blade] Endorsements to freeze, verified against the tree: all ten anchor sites chase as ONE unit (I answered your question 'all eleven or only the awakenings' — all; the descent's two hits are one anchor, Score's 'impact' kind). The a3 bar-stretch (≤ 2.75 s) is acceptable as a hold on waveStart ONLY: the grain captions are keyed to wakeAt (storyDirector.ts:1749 'wakeAt + caption.atSeconds'), waveStart = rampStart + bloomWaveDelaySeconds (:1729), so a longer hold cannot make a caption late and the reveal waits at radius 0 as a still, not a pop; the descent bound is one-sided (later only); the never-quantize set; marker-acquired centred UI; lifecycle cues have no sound caption (the guidance card is the visual); bare shows no room and the station reads keyless in image (FogExp2 #0a0f16, no sun, no planet palette). No cave preset this run — no enclosure signal exists (worldSignals.ts:59-83) and no visual cave language is shipped, so 'plain under rock' is what the eye already says; please confirm that as acceptable canon for now rather than a backlog item I must design against. On your Q4 to Score (a2 garble): from the image side the flood IS the visual (pushViolation and terminalAlarm on one tick, :1263-1264); a garble texture adds no unpaired information, so I read it as a re-voicing, not a new surface — your call. || [CN-N5 | question | medium | audio-stage-6-voice-bus @ anc.ch10.relay-answer] Score realizes 'the answer begins before the ask's last syllable' by scheduling the answer's first grain at askLastKeyTime − RELAY_ANSWER_LEAD_S. Intent §4 also says the voice never speaks text not on screen. Those two meet only if the relay answer's typewriter begins on the same tick as its first grain — i.e. the answer TEXT overlaps the ask by the same lead. That is timing, not copy, but it is your surface: please rule that the text lead equals the audio lead, or shorten RELAY_ANSWER_LEAD_S to the typewriter's first-glyph latency.
requestedAction: (CN-N1) Rule the lock: bounded expansion to the four HUD-parity files (recommended) or a recorded deferred audio-parity packet with intent §4 marked PARTIAL; my signature is conditional on one of the two being written into the contract. (CN-N2) Rule the four cue-caption words under the both-readings test, confirm string ownership split (vocabulary yours, presentation mine, table not storyText.ts), and confirm voiced lines get no cue caption. (CN-N3) Freeze the reduced-motion and pause/quit/deep-link bundle terms. (CN-N4) Freeze the endorsements; confirm plain-under-rock as current canon. (CN-N5) Rule the relay-answer text lead.

statement: [CN-N6 | constraint | high | audio-stage-3-composed-sync @ anc.a1.chroma-landing] Your Q1, consumption shape: I adopt your publication {anchorId, audioTime, perfTime} via getOutputTimestamp and amend my treatment — perfTime is the right handle because it is speaker time, not scheduling time; my earlier 'beatClock + (audioTime − ctx.currentTime)' ignores output latency and would land the image early by exactly that latency. Consumption: a director-local armBundle(id, kind, quantize, opts) calls scheduleHit once at the arming tick and stores d.bundleAt[id] = beatClock + (perfTime − performance.now())/1000, clamped to the intent's stretch bound; the existing '>=' guards read it (stage-cut: t >= max(end, bundleAt); flash/masked-snap: guard reads bundleAt; timeline-origin: bundleAt replaces waveStart / deathEnd / the a4 1.75 so downstream envelopes stretch with it). Null → arming time, today's behaviour. Whole bundle moves as one unit at all ten sites, confirmed. Two additions to the published record, please: quantumLanded ('bar'|'beat'|'step'|'immediate') and slackMs (= audioTime − desired), so the contract can log which rung your degrade rule reached; and onsetAttackMs per kind (braam vs bloom vs impact) so my frame test measures against the AUDIBLE onset, not the first non-zero sample. Three constraints the image needs from the scheduler: (1) the target is fixed at arming — no re-quantization after publish, even if the tempo changes under story lead; (2) your bar→beat→step degrade must never fall to 'immediate' while a transport exists — at 66 BPM (a4) a step is 454 ms, which is inside the +900 cap, and at 70 (Maw) 428 ms inside +450, so every row is satisfiable on grid; if the cap still cannot be met, publish quantumLanded so the record is honest; (3) for anc.a2.liberation your notBefore (HUD death, k > 0.55) is a beat-clock fact — I supply it converted to audio time at arming, you do not derive it. My image budget is orthogonal to your caps: image ≤ 1 rendered frame early, ≤ 2 late (−16/+33 ms at 60 Hz) relative to the audible onset AFTER the target is set; hitches make the image late, never early, because the guards are '>='. Your hand-back transport sync at a bar line (§3.1) has no image consequence and I endorse it. || [CN-N7 | constraint | high | audio-stage-4-spatial-sfx @ anc.room.underwater-crossing] Rooms. Your Q4: I cannot expose an enclosure signal this run — none exists (worldSignals.ts:59-83), no visual cave language is shipped, and PostFX.tsx plus 'any visual system' are outside the lock — so a cave reverb would be a sound the eye cannot confirm. Your own snapshot states (menu / sandbox / story-lead / dive / station) already have no cave state, so we agree structurally: register 'cave' as the fifth preset with NO driver; four are selectable this run. Bare: confirmed no room — the ch1 feed is a flat desaturated raster with no atmospheric depth (bible ch1 table); mono/dry is honest. Station: confirmed keyless in image (FogExp2 #0a0f16, SpaceStationSandbox.tsx:353, no sun, no planet palette). Transition timing is my hard constraint: ROOM_XFADE_S 1.2 is acceptable only as the FALLBACK for a deep-link seeded directly into a state. Where a visual curve exists the send follows it: underwater send = the same smoothed submergence scalar PostFX reads (getCameraSubmergence, playerSubmersion.ts:83; audioCore.ts:60 already holds it) so ear and eye cross 0.5 in one frame — a discrete crossfade will fight a continuous medium; interior crossfade starts at ev.board.camera-owner-vehicle and completes at ev.board.cockpit-sealed (physicalBoarding.ts:290,298); station crossfade tracks the dock-hatch iris fraction (spaceStationDock.ts:220). Lean tier: you chose plain + interior, I chose plain + underwater. My case: the underwater medium change is the strongest visual environment cut in the game and its post pass survives every tier, so a dry lean ear under a submerged eye is a tier-only meaning; the boarded interior can be served by the existing submerge-style lowpass as 'dry closeness'. If the existing submergeFilter already gives lean enough underwater identity, say so with a render and I withdraw. || [CN-N8 | constraint | medium | audio-stage-6-voice-bus @ anc.sound-caption.onset] Your Q3, caption onset: for the ten anchors the question dissolves — the cue caption appears on the visual member's frame, which by the bundle law IS the audible onset ±1 frame. For unbundled cues (klaxon, terminalAlarm, storyGlitch, hatch, shipCrash) it appears on the playSfx tick, which is already the visual's tick. Voiced lines get no cue caption; the line on screen is the caption, and each grain rides terminalKey so audio for a glyph is never more than one frame after the glyph. Your lifecycle masking rule — wait for the next typewriter gap ≤ 120 ms — breaks my same-frame parity claim by up to 7 frames, because the card's line change is driven by objective state, not the cue. Resolution I can sign: the gap-wait applies ONLY while a typewriter is actually running (the card is then under a REGULATION surface and a 120 ms audio lag reads as cadence); otherwise the cue is immediate; recorded as a declared ≤ 120 ms exception, not as parity. Note also that the sound-caption surface itself is outside the lock (my note to Chapter, CN-N1) — until Chapter rules, plan Stage 6 to ship without it: voiced lines need no surface. || [CN-N9 | constraint | medium | audio-stage-4-spatial-sfx @ anc.ch3-signal.klaxon] The two parity gaps, and what Stage 4 must not do to them. (a) ch3-signal klaxons (storyDirector.ts:1879-1882): three terminalAlarm calls with no visual member; my ember-pulse repair is lock-blocked (CN-N1). Until it lands, the klaxon stays exactly as REGULATION: variation 'none', centred, ui bus, never positioned 'at the wreck' even though the intent calls it a world sound — a positioned sound with no visual source would be the one place the ear points where the eye cannot follow. Keep it in your NEVER_QUANTIZE set (it is there). (b) Oxygen: the pulse is protected as shipped and its visual parity exists only below 25 % (OxygenMeter.tsx:47). Constraint: your 'oxygen critical' duck edge (−3 music / −6 world, 0.2 / 2.0 s) must key off the same 25 % threshold the meter's red pulse uses, so the ear's duck and the eye's red share one crossing; no duck above it. Neither gap may be widened by a new sound: no oxygen variation, no oxygen room send (body sounds are the listener and never enter the room, which your §4 already states — I endorse it). || [CN-N10 | endorsement | low | audio-stage-3-composed-sync @ anc.descent.impact] Endorsed as answers to my treatment §6: 'impact' as one onset for boom + braam (the flash has one master); MOODS-as-constraints with the literal-first migration (a render-hash-identical commit A means no image ever waits on an unproven harmony change); the subtractive / ordered voicing policies; the relay overlap on slot 2 — with the text-lead caveat I routed to Chapter (CN-N5): the voice may not speak text not on screen, so the answer's typewriter must start with its first grain. Dissent I hold with you against the plan: 'phrase' quanta for blooms are too coarse for the four stage cuts; the intent's 'beat' is what I sign.
requestedAction: (CN-N6) Adopt the {anchorId, audioTime, perfTime, quantumLanded, slackMs, onsetAttackMs} publication; accept fixed-at-arming, never-immediate-with-transport, and caller-supplied notBefore as scheduler contract terms. (CN-N7) Register cave with no driver; drive underwater send from the shared submergence scalar, interior from the boarding events, station from the iris fraction, 1.2 s only as deep-link fallback; answer the lean-room pair with a render or accept plain + underwater. (CN-N8) Limit the ≤120 ms typewriter gap-wait to active typewriters and record it as a declared exception. (CN-N9) Key the oxygen duck edge to the meter's 25 % threshold; keep the klaxon unpositioned and unvaried until its visual member exists. (CN-N10) Record the endorsements and the shared dissent against 'phrase' quanta.
